text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian commander of West African ECOMOG forces Major-General Victor Malu returns home to brief military ruler General Sani Abacha on possible military operation to dislodge soldiers who seized power in a coup in Sierra Leone.

- Dissolution of board of directors of Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Company may not be unconnected with the firm's reluctance to call off arbitration procedings against Italy's utility firm Enel over its botched $12 billion contract to buy Nigerian gas.
- Only 62,000 out of 415,427 seeking admission into Nigerian universities this year will be successful due to limited spaces.
- Lagos state government sues several firms operating in the state to court over non payment of taxes.

- Former executive secretary of Economic Commission for Africa Professor Adebayo Adedeji says Nigeria's economy remains in poor shape because of failure to build on the vision of the post civil war years after 1970.

- Nigeria's number three, chief of defence staff Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar will meet the oil minister and other senior officials of the sector next Wednesday over persistent fuel shortage in the country.
- Nation's insurance chiefs call for privatisation of NICON, the biggest insurance firm in Nigeria which is state-owned.
- Nigeria increases its troops in Freetown to 4,000 and may strike any moment from now to reinstate the democratic government toppled by junior officers in a coup in Sierra Leone last month.

- Nigeria's three multinational partners in the liquefied natural gas project -- Shell, Agip and Elf -- are meeting in London on Friday to discuss the recent dissolution of the board of directors of the LNG company.
